title: Font Stacks and Fallbacks
ques: Explain the concept of a **Font Family Stack** in CSS. Write a rule declaring a primary web font with appropriate system fallbacks and a generic family.
explanation: Font stacks define a prioritized list of fonts. If a custom web font fails to load or glyphs are missing, the browser falls back gracefully to system alternatives.

title: Text Alignment Modes
ques: Demonstrate the four primary values of **`text-align`**: `left`, `center`, `right`, and `justify`. Discuss when `justify` should be avoided for accessibility.

answer.content:
.align-left    { text-align: left; }    /* Standard LTR reading flow */
.align-center  { text-align: center; }  /* Hero headings and banners */
.align-right   { text-align: right; }   /* Numeric columns and metadata */
.align-justify { text-align: justify; } /* Newspaper-style block edges */

/* 
 * Accessibility note: 'text-align: justify' can create uneven 'rivers of white space' 
 * between words, causing reading difficulties for individuals with dyslexia.
 */

explanation: `text-align` aligns inline content within block containers. Left alignment is standard for English body text, while justified text should be used with caution.

title: Line Height and Vertical Readability
ques: Explain why **unitless line-height** values (e.g., `1.5`) are preferred over fixed pixel values (`24px`). Write an editorial typography CSS snippet.
explanation: Unitless line-height values act as relative multipliers that scale proportionally with inherited font sizes, avoiding clipping and overlap issues.

title: Letter Spacing for Typographic Hierarchy
ques: Demonstrate how to calibrate **`letter-spacing`** for uppercase subheadings and condensed display titles.
explanation: `letter-spacing` adjusts tracking. Positive letter spacing (`0.1em`) makes all-caps text readable, while subtle negative tracking (`-0.02em`) tightens large headlines.
